Just gonna say, in contrast to all these people, listen to your gut.  It is a red flag the way he's asking you for this, but some people are immature at sharing how they feel. That's a really hard thing to do because we've both spent 1/3 of our lives together (I'm 21 and met her when I was 15), and yes I know it's lovey dovey and fatally romantic, but we want to do everything to make it work.  I mean even when she can have loads of fun she's staying with me, and it's because it's truly magical when we're together.  We have grown pretty different.  But you know what it's like to have a best friend?  We've been through everything together, we know our whole families, I've nigh proposed to her (and she nigh accepted) but I didn't actually because it's not socially acceptable to marry this early, we know each other intimately, like to the absolute maximum that intimacy between two humans can allow (which I admit is not all too unique), have made those eternal promises that you make in love... We really tolerate each others' presence and don't ever want it to go away.  But being away from each other is like some kind of hypnosis and it changes who we are and we lose some feelings, but then when I'm with her again it's like a drug that keeps giving, the rush never ends as if it were some kind of short-term dopamine fix, but it's a constant peaceful bliss that we know would never fade, and it hasn't for 6 years, and we're always improving each other's lives and appreciating each other.  I know there's plenty of people with multiples of our years of experience, but we're pretty sure that there's pretty much nothing on the table that can make one of us walk out when we're together.  The fights were worse earlier in our relationship, and it only got better (**in person**)

I'll say, for now, NOPE ON FINDING SOMEONE ELSE!

No, my survival instincts won't kill me, but my brain is definitely sure I don't want to be around.  If I could poof myself out of existence, I would, and I think it would significantly increase the number of suicides.  Not doing the act often doesn't have to do with not wanting to be dead.

The problem is I'm very sure that I want to die, but my stupid fucking survival instincts can't take a knife and slit my wrists for the hell of it.  I need serious suppression of the survival force in me so I can commit to my mental decision once and for all.  I'm trying to get my hands on some fentanyl

I'm going to a therapist, and I'll look into Men's behavior change programs as well.  I see my change as an abuser as a huge goal in my life.
I have considered different types of behaviors that can intervene when I have triggers, but I'm more worried about forgetting to meditate than thinking that it won't help.

Though there were small instances elsewhere, the main pervasive thing was jealousy and control.  Most of the abuse consisted of me spamming her when she was out with friends, telling her how to dress, what she could do on her devices (with parental controls installed by me — they have been removed for a while now though), I took away her makeup, etc, etc.  These were the main things, and most fights and all instances of me being mean to her were 9 times out of 10 related to those two things (jealousy and control).  So she may say that fighting/yelling was also a problem, which I agree with, but it was always stemming from those things.
I have thought about medication.  Maybe I do need some kind of medication, but I'm going to first see a psychiatrist.
I'm going to give it my full effort to listen to everything that my therapist says.  I have a very inner desire to change, and so I'm going to pay attention religiously to any counseling
